points.place: 美国康涅狄格州哈特福德
points.title: 童年与教育启蒙
points.description: 1902年6月16日，芭芭拉·麦克林托克出生于康涅狄格州哈特福德的一个家庭。她是家中第三个孩子，父亲是医生，母亲是艺术家。麦克林托克从小就展现出对自然和科学的浓厚兴趣，尤其热爱植物学。在康涅狄格州埃文斯中学期间，她表现出色，1919年毕业后进入康奈尔大学农学院学习植物学。这段早期教育为她后来在遗传学领域的突破奠定了坚实基础，培养了她的观察力和对细节的敏锐感知。
points.descriptionEn: Born on June 16, 1902, in Hartford, Connecticut, Barbara McClintock was the third child in a family of four. Her father was a physician and her mother an artist. From an early age, McClintock showed a strong interest in nature and science, particularly botany. During her time at Erasmus Hall High School in Brooklyn, she excelled academically and graduated in 1919. She then entered the College of Agriculture at Cornell University to study botany. This early education laid the foundation for her later breakthroughs in genetics and developed her keen observation skills and attention to detail.

points.title: 康奈尔大学研究生阶段
points.description: 在康奈尔大学，麦克林托克继续深造，专注于植物遗传学研究。她师从植物学家C.B.哈钦森，成为该校首位获得植物学博士学位的女性。在此期间，她与同事共同发现了玉米染色体的交叉现象，并开发出一种技术，可以在显微镜下追踪染色体的变化。这一研究成果奠定了她在遗传学领域的声誉。1927年，她获得洛克菲勒奖学金，得以继续研究。康奈尔大学的经历不仅塑造了她的科学方法，也培养了她独立思考和挑战传统观念的勇气。
points.descriptionEn: At Cornell University, McClintock pursued advanced studies in plant genetics, working under botanist C.B. Hutchison. She became the first woman to earn a Ph.D. in botany from the institution. During this time, she and colleagues discovered the phenomenon of chromosome crossing in corn and developed techniques to track chromosome changes under the microscope. This research established her reputation in the field of genetics. In 1927, she received a Rockefeller Fellowship to continue her work. Her time at Cornell not only shaped her scientific methodology but also fostered her courage to think independently and challenge conventional wisdom.

points.placeEn: Cold Spring Harbor, New York, United States
points.title: 冷泉港实验室研究
points.titleEn: Research at Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory
points.description: 1927年，麦克林托克加入冷泉港实验室，开始了长达数十年的玉米遗传学研究。在这里，她详细绘制了玉米的染色体图谱，发现了转座子（或称'跳跃基因'）的存在。她观察到某些基因可以在染色体上移动，影响其他基因的表达。这一发现挑战了当时遗传学界普遍认为基因位置固定的观念。尽管她的研究成果在当时难以被同行理解和接受，麦克林托克坚持自己的观察和结论。冷泉港时期是她科学创造力最为旺盛的阶段，为后来获得诺贝尔奖奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1927, McClintock joined the Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory, where she would conduct corn genetics research for decades. Here, she meticulously mapped corn chromosomes and discovered the existence of transposable elements (or 'jumping genes'). She observed that certain genes could move along chromosomes, affecting the expression of other genes. This discovery challenged the prevailing view in genetics that genes had fixed positions. Despite her findings being difficult for contemporaries to understand and accept, McClintock坚持ed her observations and conclusions. Her time at Cold Spring Harbor represented her most scientifically creative period, laying the foundation for her later Nobel Prize.

points.place: 美国密苏里州圣路易斯
points.title: 卡内基研究所时期
points.description: 1941年，麦克林托克加入位于密苏里州圣路易斯的卡内基研究所，继续研究玉米遗传学。在第二次世界大战期间，她的研究因战争而受到一定影响，但她仍坚持工作。1951年，她在冷泉港举行的遗传学研讨会上首次公开提出转座子理论，但这一理论在当时并未得到广泛认可。尽管面临同行的质疑和孤立，麦克林托克继续完善她的理论，并在1953年发表了重要论文。这一时期，她开始转向研究南美洲玉米的遗传多样性，为理解玉米进化提供了新视角。卡内基研究所的经历锻炼了她在逆境中坚持科学信念的毅力。
points.descriptionEn: In 1941, McClintock joined the Carnegie Institution in St. Louis, Missouri, continuing her research in corn genetics. During World War II, her research was somewhat affected by the war, but she persisted in her work. In 1951, she first publicly presented her theory of transposable elements at a genetics symposium at Cold Spring Harbor, but the theory was not widely accepted at the time. Despite facing skepticism and isolation from peers, McClintock continued to refine her theory and published a significant paper in 1953. During this period, she shifted to studying the genetic diversity of South American corn, providing new perspectives on corn evolution. Her time at the Carnegie Institution strengthened her perseverance in maintaining scientific信念 despite adversity.

points.placeEn: Cold Spring Harbor, New York, United States
points.title: 晚年与诺贝尔奖
points.description: 1967年，麦克林托克回到冷泉港实验室，继续她的研究工作。直到1980年代，分子生物学的发展才证实了她的转座子理论的正确性。1983年，81岁高龄的麦克林托克因发现遗传转座子机制而获得诺贝尔生理学或医学奖，成为历史上首位单独获得该奖项的女性科学家。晚年，她成为科学界的标志性人物，经常受邀演讲和分享她的科学哲学。她强调科学直觉和观察的重要性，认为真正的科学发现往往来自于对细节的敏锐观察。1992年9月2日，麦克林托克在冷泉港逝世，享年90岁，为科学界留下宝贵的遗产。
points.descriptionEn: In 1967, McClintock returned to Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory, continuing her research. It wasn't until the 1980s, with advances in molecular biology, that her theory of transposable elements was finally confirmed. In 1983, at the age of 81, McClintock was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for her discovery of genetic transposition, becoming the first woman to receive the prize unshared. In her later years, she became an iconic figure in science, frequently invited to lecture and share her scientific philosophy. She emphasized the importance of scientific intuition and observation, arguing that true scientific discoveries often come from keen attention to detail. On September 2, 1992, McClintock died in Cold Spring Harbor at the age of 90, leaving a lasting legacy to the scientific community.

supporter.zh: 麦克林托克被视为科学界的先驱和独立思考的典范。她坚持自己的科学发现，即使面对同行的质疑和孤立也不放弃，展现了科学家的坚定信念和勇气。她的转座子理论彻底改变了人们对基因结构的理解，为现代分子生物学奠定了基础。作为一位在男性主导的科学领域取得卓越成就的女性，她打破了性别壁垒，激励了无数后辈科学家。她的故事体现了科学发现的本质：真正的突破往往来自于对传统观念的挑战和对细节的敏锐观察。
supporter.en: McClintock is regarded as a pioneer in science and a model of independent thinking. She坚持ed her scientific findings despite skepticism and isolation from peers, demonstrating the conviction and courage of a true scientist. Her theory of transposable elements revolutionized understanding of gene structure and laid the foundation for modern molecular biology. As a woman achieving excellence in a male-dominated field, she broke gender barriers and inspired countless future scientists. Her story embodies the essence of scientific discovery: true breakthroughs often come from challenging conventional wisdom and keen observation of details.

critic.zh: 批评者认为麦克林托克在早期未能有效沟通她的理论，导致其发现被推迟认可数十年。有人指出她过于依赖直觉和观察，缺乏系统的实验验证，这在当时的技术条件下是合理的限制。此外，她专注于玉米遗传学研究，被认为研究领域过于狭窄，未能将她的发现更广泛地应用于其他生物系统。批评者也指出，尽管她后来获得诺贝尔奖，但她的科学方法在当代高度依赖技术的环境中可能显得过时，强调直觉而非数据驱动的研究方法在现代科学中已不再主流。
critic.en: Critics argue that McClintock failed to effectively communicate her theory in its early stages, leading to decades of delayed recognition. Some point out her over-reliance on intuition and observation, lacking systematic experimental validation, which was a reasonable limitation given the technological constraints of her time. Additionally, her focus on corn genetics is seen as too narrow, as she didn't more broadly apply her findings to other biological systems. Critics also note that despite her later Nobel Prize, her scientific methods may appear outdated in today's technology-dependent environment, as her intuitive rather than data-driven approach is no longer mainstream in contemporary science.

objective.zh: 历史学界将麦克林托克定义为20世纪最具影响力的遗传学家之一，她的发现代表了科学史上从经典遗传学到分子生物学的重要转折点。在流行文化中，她常被描绘为'孤独的天才'形象，象征着科学发现的孤独与坚持。她的故事被广泛用于讨论科学范式转变、性别在科学中的地位以及科学发现的本质。麦克林托克的工作不仅推动了遗传学的发展，也为理解基因调控、发育生物学和进化论提供了新视角。她的经历成为科学社会学的重要案例，展示了科学共识形成的过程以及创新思想如何最终获得认可。
objective.en: Historians define McClintock as one of the most influential geneticists of the 20th century, with her discoveries representing a crucial turning point in the history of science from classical genetics to molecular biology. In popular culture, she is often portrayed as a 'lonely genius' figure, symbolizing the solitude and perseverance of scientific discovery. Her story is widely used to discuss scientific paradigm shifts, gender in science, and the nature of scientific discovery. McClintock's work not only advanced genetics but also provided new perspectives on gene regulation, developmental biology, and evolution. Her experience has become an important case study in the sociology of science, illustrating how scientific consensus forms and innovative ideas eventually gain recognition.

self.zh: 如果你知道你在做什么，那么你就不必担心别人怎么想。
self.en: If you know what you are doing, then you don't have to worry about what other people think.

others.zh: 麦克林托克的工作是20世纪生物学中最伟大的成就之一，它彻底改变了我们对基因如何运作的理解。
others.en: McClintock's work is one of the greatest achievements in 20th-century biology; it revolutionized our understanding of how genes work.
